name: MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard
title: UnsavedChangesGuard
wrapsNative: ViewModifier using interactiveDismissDisabled, navigationBarBackButtonHidden with a toolbar back button (iOS), confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:actions:message:) and alert for a failed save
summary: A modifier that warns before leaving a screen or a sheet throws away unsaved changes, with Keep editing, Discard changes and an optional Save and leave.
whenToUse: On an editor or a form in a sheet or a pushed screen, while it has changes that are not saved and leaving would lose them.
whenNotToUse: When changes are saved as they are made (show MonarchSaveStatusIndicator instead), or when the draft is kept and restored later. For confirming a deletion use confirm-dialog.
api: func monarchUnsavedChangesGuard(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, hasChanges: Bool, labels: MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLabels = MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLabels(), guardsBackButton: Bool = true, onSave: (@MainActor () async throws -> Void)? = nil, onLeave: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLeaveReason) -> Void) -> some View

MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard.init(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, hasChanges: Bool, labels: MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLabels = MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLabels(), guardsBackButton: Bool = true, onSave: (@MainActor () async throws -> Void)? = nil, onLeave: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLeaveReason) -> Void)

MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLabels.init(title: String? = nil, message: String? = nil, keepEditing: String? = nil, discard: String? = nil, save: String? = nil, saveFailed: String? = nil, back: String? = nil, saving: String? = nil)

options.name: isPresented
options.description: Whether the question is shown. Set it to true from the app's own Cancel or Close button when there are changes; the guarding back button sets it too.

options.name: hasChanges
options.description: Whether there are unsaved changes. While false nothing is blocked and the system back button is kept.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the question, the message, the three choices, the save failure, the back button and "Saving".

options.name: guardsBackButton
options.description: Whether the navigation bar's back button is replaced, while there are changes, by one that asks first. iOS only.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Saves the changes. When given, Save and leave is offered. While it runs the screen cannot be left; a thrown error is shown in an alert and the person stays.

options.name: onLeave
options.description: Leaves the screen (dismiss or pop), called with .discard straight away or with .save after onSave succeeded.

states.name: no changes
states.description: Nothing changes: the sheet can be swiped away and the system back button works.

states.name: changes
states.description: The sheet cannot be swiped away, and on iOS the back button reads "Back" with a chevron and asks first; the back swipe is off.

states.name: asking
states.description: A confirmation dialog titled "Discard unsaved changes?" with Save and leave, Discard changes (destructive) and Keep editing (cancel).

states.name: saving
states.description: A "Saving" progress indicator on a raised surface over the content; leaving stays blocked.

states.name: save failed
states.description: An alert with the error's description, or "Your changes could not be saved. Try again.", and a Keep editing button.

appearance: The question and the failure are the system confirmation dialog and alert, drawn by the system in every theme; the destructive choice is the system's red. The saving indicator uses the raised background, the default text colour and a medium shadow from the theme.
platformNotes: The web UnsavedChangesGuard is a dialog plus a hook that blocks router navigation, intercepts same-origin links and asks the browser to warn before the tab closes. iOS has no links or tabs to close, so the guard blocks the two ways out a person can take without the app's code, the sheet swipe and the back button, and the app's own Cancel button sets isPresented. SwiftUI cannot tell when a blocked swipe was attempted, so a swipe does nothing instead of asking. The web keeps the dialog open with a pending state while saving; the system dialog closes when a button is tapped, so the guard shows a progress indicator over the screen and reports a failure in an alert. The web's children (extra content in the dialog) cannot go in a confirmation dialog. Android builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: System behaviour: VoiceOver reads the dialog's title and message; the escape gesture chooses Keep editing, the cancel role.
The destructive choice is named "Discard changes", so it does not depend on its red colour.
The replacement back button is a labelled button with a backward chevron that follows the reading direction.
"Saving" is announced when the save starts and shown with a labelled progress indicator; a failure is shown in an alert, which VoiceOver reads.
While leaving is blocked, the back swipe and the sheet swipe are off, so a gesture cannot lose the changes.
edgeCases: Without onSave only Discard changes and Keep editing are offered.
Apply the modifier inside the sheet's content (for example on the root of its NavigationStack), so interactiveDismissDisabled reaches the sheet.
Errors are shown with their LocalizedError description when they have one; other errors show the built-in failure text.
The guard does not stop the app from dismissing in code; route every Cancel and Close through isPresented.

examples.title: Leaving with unsaved changes
A pushed screen whose back button asks first
examples.code:
TextField("Notes", text: $notes, axis: .vertical)
    .monarchTextStyle(.body)
    .navigationTitle("Notes")
    .monarchUnsavedChangesGuard(
        isPresented: $isAsking,
        hasChanges: !notes.isEmpty,
        onLeave: { _ in dismiss() }
    )

parityExceptions.reason: The question is the system confirmation dialog. Anchored to its button it is a bubble with the two actions; Keep editing is its cancel role, which the system does not draw as a button there (tapping outside or the escape gesture keeps editing). The destructive role takes the system red.
parityExceptions.convention: HIG: confirmation dialog; the cancel role is the dismissal
